quizzes.title: MCQ: What are cryptarithms?
quizzes.instructions: Recall the rules of cryptarithm puzzles.

questions.prompt: In a cryptarithm, two different letters must stand for:
questions.explanation: Different letters must stand for different digits; the same letter always means the same digit.

questions.prompt: Which digit can never be the first digit of a multi-digit number in a cryptarithm?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not written in standard numbers, so the leading letter must be 1–9.

questions.prompt: Which column of a cryptarithm should be analysed first?

options.text: Any column — order makes no difference

questions.explanation: Column addition starts at the units, and its carry feeds the next column — so work right to left.

quizzes.title: MCQ: Cryptarithm strategies
quizzes.instructions: Use column equations, carry bounds and parity.

questions.prompt: In a two-addend column, what is the largest possible carry out?
questions.explanation: 9 + 9 + 1 = 19 at most, so the carry out is at most 1.
10A + B + 10B + A = 11A + 11B = 11(A + B) — always a multiple of 11.

questions.prompt: If AB + BA = DD with D even, what can parity tell us about A and B?

options.text: They must have the same parity (both even or both odd)

questions.explanation: DD even forces 11(A + B) even, so A + B must be even — which happens exactly when A and B share their parity.

quizzes.title: MCQ: Classic cryptarithms
quizzes.instructions: Solve column by column, then verify.

questions.prompt: For AB + BA = 66, which digit pairs (A, B) work?

options.text: Any pair with A + B = 6, A ≠ B, A ≥ 1

questions.explanation: 11(A + B) = 66 gives A + B = 6; pairs like (1,5), (2,4), (4,2), (5,1) all work — (3,3) is banned and (6,0) makes B? A = 6, B = 0 gives 60 + 06 — the leading zero of 06 is not allowed.

questions.prompt: What is 25 + 52 in the AB + BA pattern?
A cryptarithm is examined and no assignment of digits works. The correct conclusion is:

options.text: You must have made an arithmetic error — a solution always exists
The puzzle is impossible, and a reasoned proof of that is a valid answer
Letters may share digits after all

questions.explanation: Some cryptarithms are deliberately impossible; demonstrating that with complete reasoning counts as solving the puzzle.
